LESSON: RHYTHMIC

Grade: PP2
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Rhythmic

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Rhythmic. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify musical instruments used for performing rhythmic patterns e.g. percussion
2. display the ability to create rhythmic movements through dance, nodding and swaying for enjoyment 105
3. create rhythm using percussion instruments to enhance tempo
4. appreciate others talent as they perform rhythmic patterns using percussion instruments rhythmic patterns using percussion instruments self and others talents Core-Competence

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. identify musical instruments used for performing rhythmic patterns e.g. percussion
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to identify musical instruments used for performing rhythmic patterns e.g. percussion. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. display the ability to create rhythmic movements through dance, nodding and swaying for enjoyment 105
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to display the ability to create rhythmic movements through dance, nodding and swaying for enjoyment 105. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. create rhythm using percussion instruments to enhance tempo
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to create rhythm using percussion instruments to enhance tempo. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

4. appreciate others talent as they perform rhythmic patterns using percussion instruments rhythmic patterns using percussion instruments self and others talents Core-Competence
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to appreciate others talent as they perform rhythmic patterns using percussion instruments rhythmic patterns using percussion instruments self and others talents Core-Competence. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Rhythmic.
2. Explain Rhythmic to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Rhythmic.
4. Show that you can: identify musical instruments used for performing rhythmic patterns e.g. percussion
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Rhythmic. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Rhythmic important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. identify musical instruments used for performing rhythmic patterns e.g. percussion
2. display the ability to create rhythmic movements through dance, nodding and swaying for enjoyment 105
3. create rhythm using percussion instruments to enhance tempo
4. appreciate others talent as they perform rhythmic patterns using percussion instruments rhythmic patterns using percussion instruments self and others talents Core-Competence

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
